notes: §1985:XII.3.4 GR11 (kb/Work PB5382, PB5887, landed): the lines a REPLACE introduces take the indicator of the line the replaced text begins on: CopyProcessor.ApplyReplacements writes the debugging-line carrier on each introduced line when that line is a debugging line, so DebuggingLineRewriter keeps or hides every introduced line. When it is a source line, whether a line pseudo-text-2 writes as a debugging line stays one the 1985 text leaves open: GR11 can be read to give it the replaced line's indicator (reading P, kb/Work PB5382's), or, as the same sentence must be read in COPY beside §1985:XII.2.4 GR9's 'only those text words that are specified on debugging lines where the debugging line is within pseudo-text-2 appear on debugging lines in the resultant program', to speak only of the additional lines a placement creates (reading Q); GR8 only permits debugging lines in pseudo-text. CLAUDE.md rule 1's precedence chooses Q, as GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 does (determination D-85-REPLACE-DEBUGGING-LINES, docs/conformance/3/), and §1985:VI.7.3 makes the line a comment line when WITH DEBUGGING MODE is absent. A literal placed on a debugging line that the program-text area cannot hold from its area's margin (65 positions in area A, 61 in area B) draws COBOL7039. Witnesses: pb5382-replace-debugging-introduced-lines (1, ONE, THREE at 85), pb5887-replace-pseudo-text-debugging-line (S1, S2, S3, N=1 at 85), pb5382-replace-literal-on-debugging-line (COBOL7039), 1985-GR-XII_3_4-11 (the long literal on a source line still runs).

next.reason: 1985: "the indicator area of the introduced lines contains the same character as the line on which the text being replaced begins"; 2023: "shall be in logical free-form reference format. Text-words inserted ... are placed in accordance with the rules of free-form reference format". Same subject, placing inserted text, but 2023 uses logical free-form: no indicator area, no added continuation lines, no error for a literal continued onto a debugging line.
